prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- In a television interview, the mother of a man charged in the murder of an Auburn University freshman repeatedly says she's sorry about the suffering the victim's family is enduring. Courtney Larrell Lockhart was arrested Friday in Phenix City, Alabama, about 35 miles from Auburn. "I never thought Courtney would do this. I never, never thought," Courtney Larrell Lockhart's mother Catherine Williams told CNN affiliate WRBL on Saturday. "But I'm sorry for that family and I'm sorry. I'm just sorry," she said. "I got nothing else to say. I'm just sorry for the loss of that family." Police announced Saturday that they had arrested Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, in connection with the shooting death of Lauren Burk, 18, of Marietta, Georgia.  Watch the mother cry and apologize » . Lockhart faces charges of capital murder during a kidnapping, capital murder during a robbery and capital murder during an attempted rape, police said. Also, Lockhart is facing robbery charges in the Phenix City, Alabama, area, said William Clanton of the Phenix City Police Department. Clanton did not know how many robberies Lockhart was suspected of committing. Lockhart is being held in the Russell County jail, but is expected to be moved to Lee County soon, where Auburn University is, Clanton said. Burk was found shot Tuesday night on North College Street, a few miles north of campus. She died later at a hospital. Minutes after police responded to a call reporting an injured person and found Burk, they received a report of a car -- which turned out to be Burk's -- on fire in a campus parking lot. Authorities believe gasoline or another accelerant was used to ignite Burk's car, Auburn Assistant Police Chief Tommy Dawson said Friday. Police were investigating whether a gas can found in downtown Auburn was related to the case. Memorial services for Burk were held Saturday and Sunday at a Marietta church and synagogue. A campus-wide memorial service will be held Monday. A memorial service was held Sunday in Athens, Georgia, for another slain university student Eve Carson, the Athens Banner Herald reported. Carson, 22, the student body president for the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, was found shot to death in a suburban neighborhood not far from campus about 5 a.m. Wednesday. Her car was found Thursday, in another neighborhood to the west, about a block or two from where she lived with roommates. On Saturday, police released two surveillance photographs of a "person of interest" taken by an ATM camera in the Chapel Hill area, Chapel Hill Police Chief Brian Curran said. The person appeared to be using one of Carson's ATM cards and was driving a vehicle that was possibly hers. Curran called the photographs the "biggest break" in the case, which he said still appears to be random. Reminders of the popular student president appeared on the jerseys of the university's men's basketball team Saturday night as they took on Duke University's Blue Devils in Durham, North Carolina. The top-ranked Tar Heels wore jersey patches that read "Eve." Many of Duke's fans donned small light-blue ribbons as a show of support. There was a moment of silence for Carson before tip-off. The ribbons and moment of silence say "a heckuva lot about Duke University," UNC Coach Roy Williams told reporters after the game. The Tar Heels won 76-68. E-mail to a friend .

**(CNN) —** In a television interview, the mother of a man charged with murdering an Auburn University freshman repeatedly expressed sorrow for the suffering endured by the victim’s family.

Courtney Larrell Lockhart was arrested Friday in Phenix City, Alabama, approximately 35 miles from Auburn.

“I never thought Courtney would do this. I never, never thought,” Lockhart’s mother, Catherine Williams, told CNN affiliate WRBL on Saturday.

“But I’m sorry for that family, and I’m sorry. I’m just sorry,” she said. “I got nothing else to say. I’m just sorry for the loss of that family.”

Police announced Saturday that they had arrested Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, in connection with the shooting death of Lauren Burk, 18, of Marietta, Georgia.

**Watch the mother cry and apologize »**

Lockhart faces charges of capital murder during a kidnapping, capital murder during a robbery, and capital murder during an attempted rape, police said.

He also faces robbery charges in the Phenix City area, according to William Clanton of the Phenix City Police Department. Clanton said he did not know how many robberies Lockhart was suspected of committing.

Lockhart is being held in the Russell County Jail but is expected to be transferred soon to Lee County, where Auburn University is located, Clanton said.

Burk was found with a gunshot wound Tuesday night on North College Street, a few miles north of campus. She later died at a hospital.

Minutes after responding to a report of an injured person and finding Burk, police received another report of a car on fire in a campus parking lot. The vehicle was later identified as Burk’s.

Authorities believe gasoline or another accelerant was used to set Burk’s car on fire, Auburn Assistant Police Chief Tommy Dawson said Friday. Police were investigating whether a gas can found in downtown Auburn was connected to the case.

Memorial services for Burk were held Saturday and Sunday at a Marietta church and synagogue. A campus-wide memorial service was scheduled for Monday.

A memorial service was also held Sunday in Athens, Georgia, for another slain university student, Eve Carson, the *Athens Banner-Herald* reported.

Carson, 22, the student body president at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, was found shot to death in a suburban neighborhood not far from campus at about 5 a.m. Wednesday.

Her car was found Thursday in another neighborhood to the west, approximately one or two blocks from the home she shared with roommates.

On Saturday, police released two surveillance photographs of a “person of interest” captured by an ATM camera in the Chapel Hill area, Chapel Hill Police Chief Brian Curran said. The person appeared to be using one of Carson’s ATM cards and was driving a vehicle that may have been hers.

Curran described the photographs as the “biggest break” in the case, which he said still appeared to be random.

Reminders of the popular student body president appeared on the jerseys of the university’s men’s basketball team Saturday night as the team faced the Duke University Blue Devils in Durham, North Carolina.

The top-ranked Tar Heels wore jersey patches bearing the name “Eve.” Many Duke fans wore small light-blue ribbons as a show of support, and a moment of silence was observed for Carson before tip-off.

The ribbons and moment of silence said “a heckuva lot about Duke University,” UNC Coach Roy Williams told reporters after the game.

The Tar Heels won 76–68.

Courtney Larrell Lockhart was taken into custody Friday in Phenix City, Alabama, roughly 35 miles from Auburn.

Authorities announced Saturday that Lockhart, a 23-year-old resident of Smiths, Alabama, had been arrested in connection with the fatal shooting of Lauren Burk. Burk, 18, was an Auburn freshman from Marietta, Georgia.

Police said Lockhart is charged with capital murder committed during a kidnapping, capital murder committed during a robbery, and capital murder committed during an attempted rape.

William Clanton of the Phenix City Police Department said Lockhart also faces robbery charges in the Phenix City area. Clanton could not say how many robberies investigators believed Lockhart may have committed.

Lockhart remains in the Russell County jail, though he is expected to be transferred soon to Lee County, where Auburn University is located, according to Clanton.

Burk was discovered Tuesday night with a gunshot wound on North College Street, several miles north of the Auburn campus. She later died at a hospital.

Only minutes after officers responded to a report of an injured person and found Burk, police were notified that a vehicle was burning in a university parking lot. The car was later identified as Burk’s.

Auburn Assistant Police Chief Tommy Dawson said Friday that investigators believe gasoline or some other accelerant was used to set the vehicle ablaze. Authorities were also examining whether a gasoline can discovered in downtown Auburn was connected to the investigation.

Services honoring Burk took place Saturday and Sunday at a church and a synagogue in Marietta. Auburn planned a memorial for the entire campus on Monday.

Meanwhile, another memorial was held Sunday in Athens, Georgia, for slain college student Eve Carson, according to the *Athens Banner-Herald*.

Carson, 22, served as student body president at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. Her body was found at about 5 a.m. Wednesday in a residential area near the campus; she had been shot to death.

Her vehicle was recovered Thursday in a neighborhood farther west, approximately one or two blocks from the home she shared with roommates.

On Saturday, Chapel Hill police made public two surveillance images of a person they wanted to question. Police Chief Brian Curran said the pictures had been captured by an ATM camera in the Chapel Hill area.

The individual shown in the images appeared to be using one of Carson’s bank cards and was behind the wheel of a vehicle that may have belonged to her. Curran described the photographs as the investigation’s most important development so far. He added that the killing continued to appear random.

Tributes to the well-liked student leader were visible Saturday night when UNC’s men’s basketball team faced the Duke University Blue Devils in Durham, North Carolina.

The No. 1-ranked Tar Heels wore patches bearing the name “Eve” on their uniforms. Many Duke supporters displayed small light-blue ribbons in solidarity, and the arena observed a moment of silence for Carson before the game began.

Afterward, UNC Coach Roy Williams told journalists that the ribbons and the pregame silence reflected very positively on Duke University.

North Carolina defeated Duke 76-68.

counterfactuals.output:
**AUBURN, Ala. —** Police arrested an Alabama man in connection with the abduction and fatal shooting of Auburn University freshman Lauren Burk, whose killing sent shock waves through the campus and prompted an intensive multiagency investigation.

Courtney Larrell Lockhart, 23, of Smiths Station, was taken into custody in the Phenix City area after a traffic stop and pursuit, authorities said. He was charged with capital murder in Burk’s death and was being held without bond. The capital charge alleged that the killing occurred during a kidnapping.

Burk, an 18-year-old from Marietta, Georgia, was found Tuesday night, March 4, 2008, along Alabama Highway 147, several miles from Auburn’s campus. She had suffered a gunshot wound and was taken to East Alabama Medical Center, where she died. Investigators later found her black Honda Civic burning in a campus parking lot.

Authorities said evidence recovered after Lockhart’s arrest linked him to the crime, though they declined at the time to disclose all details. Police searched property and examined weapons and other potential evidence as they worked to reconstruct Burk’s movements and determine whether robbery or sexual assault had been part of the attack.

Auburn officials increased security and urged students to remain cautious while investigators searched for a suspect. News of the arrest brought some relief, but students and faculty continued mourning Burk, who had enrolled at the university only months earlier.

Lockhart’s arrest did not constitute a finding of guilt. Prosecutors would be required to prove the allegations in court.

### Eve Carson investigation continues in North Carolina

The Auburn arrest came as police in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, pursued leads in the separate killing of University of North Carolina student body president Eve Marie Carson.

Carson, 22, was found shot to death early March 5 in a residential area near the UNC campus. Police said she had been shot multiple times. Her sport-utility vehicle was missing when her body was discovered but was recovered later.

Investigators released surveillance photographs taken at an automated teller machine showing a person attempting to use Carson’s bank card. Police appealed to the public for help identifying the individual and tracing Carson’s movements during the hours before her death. Authorities emphasized that the photograph was an important lead but cautioned against assuming guilt solely from the image.

Carson, a senior from Athens, Georgia, was widely known at UNC for her campus leadership, volunteer work and academic achievements. Vigils and memorial gatherings drew thousands of students, faculty members and local residents.

### UNC and Duke pause rivalry to honor the victims

Grief over Carson’s death reached beyond Chapel Hill to Duke University, UNC’s longtime athletic rival. Before the schools’ men’s basketball game at Cameron Indoor Stadium, the crowd observed a moment of silence.

The tribute also remembered Abhijit Mahato, a Duke graduate engineering student who had been found shot to death in his off-campus apartment earlier that year. The observance briefly set aside one of college basketball’s fiercest rivalries, with students, players and coaches joining in remembrance of both victims.

UNC and Duke representatives said the gesture reflected the close ties between the two university communities. The game went forward, but the memorial underscored that the recent violence had affected both campuses far beyond athletics.
